newsitem.title: USA: Riddell to buy Varsity Spirit.
newsitem.headline: Riddell to buy Varsity Spirit.

text.p: Sporting goods maker Riddell Sports Inc said it signed a definitive agreement to buy Varsity Spirit Corp, which makes cheeleading and dance uniforms, for about $91 million in cash, or $18.90 a share.
Memphis, Tennessee-based Varsity Spirit, which had revenues of about $90 million in 1996, is also the leading cheerleading and dance camp operator in the U.S.
New York-based Riddell, best known as a maker of football equipment, said it will pay for the acquisition through the placement of senior notes.
The company also has a commitment for $100 million of bridge financing, as well as a revolving credit facility of $35 million, it said.
Jeffrey Webb, Varsity Spirit's chairman, president and chief executive, will become vice-chairman of Riddell after the acquisition, Riddell said.
The new Riddell, based on year-end 1996 figures, will have revenues of about $160 million and assets of about $180 million, the company added.
